newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-PIOLINE BEATS FURLAN TO PUT FRANCE LEVEL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PIOLINE BEATS FURLAN TO PUT FRANCE LEVEL.

text.p: France, 2-0 down on the first day, levelled their Davis Cup world group semfinal at 2-2 when Cedric Pioline achieved a four-set victory over Renzo Furlan on Sunday.
The French number one made a dramatic improvement on his limp performance in defeat by Andrea Gaudenzi in Friday's first singles to beat Furlan 6-3 2-6 6-2 6-4 in just over three hours.
France's second point followed their straight-sets doubles win on Saturday after the shock of losing both opening singles on Friday.

Pioline, at number 17 the highest world ranked player of the tie, served much better, showed a lot more mobility and was more patient in the long rallies preferred by the Italian slow-court specialists.
Backed by a small but enthusiastic home crowd, Pioline also showed far more passion than on Friday. Having disappointed the fans two days earlier, he now had to win to keep his country in the tie.
The winners will play away to Sweden, victors over the Czech Republic, in the final on the last weekend of November.
The battling Furlan, dubbed the "Italian Chang" because of his small stature and fighting spirit, started with two double faults in his first service game to allow Pioline a break and a 2-0 lead.
The Italian number one, ranked 38, saved four set points on his service in the eighth game but lost the next game to concede the first set in 50 minutes.

Furlan broke Pioline in the sixth game of the second set on his way to pulling level at 1-1 but Pioline showed he meant business by breaking Furlan in the Italian's first service game of the third set.
Pioline broke Furlan again with a fine lob which the Italian just failed to reach in the fifth game of that set.
Furlan, whose four-set victory over Arnaud Boetsch gave underdogs Italy their 2-0 lead on Friday, saved two break points in the opening game of the fourth set.
But Pioline brilliantly won a long rally to go 30-15 up in the third and made the crucial break in that game when Furlan netted a superb return by the Frenchman.
Pioline won with an ace on his second match point.
